name: Clopidogrel
reviewed_by: William Gregory M. Rivero, MD, FPCP, DPSN
drafted_by: AI-assisted draft (Claude) for review by Dr. W. Rivero

key_interactions.effect: Significantly reduce the antiplatelet effect of clopidogrel, even 12 hours apart (label).
key_interactions.action: Avoid; pantoprazole, lansoprazole and dexlansoprazole had less effect (label).

key_interactions.effect: More active metabolite and platelet inhibition; higher bleeding risk (label).
Repaglinide exposure rises 3.9- to 5.1-fold (strong CYP2C8 inhibition) (label).
key_interactions.action: Avoid; if unavoidable, start repaglinide at 0.5 mg before each meal, maximum 4 mg/day, and monitor glucose more often.
In acute coronary syndrome needing opioids, consider a parenteral antiplatelet agent.

key_interactions.effect: Higher bleeding risk, including gastrointestinal bleeding (label).

key_interactions.action: Promptly evaluate any signs of blood loss.
